title: Sourcing App With Curate Document And Beams Windows Slabs Modules
description: Create a new app technology `sourcing` for handpicking and curating 3D object kinds (not instances) out of a catalogue. Each object kind has an availability count and follows a typology (tree). Sourcing has modules (beams, windows, slabs) contributed as separate plugin crates via a new Contribution::SourcingModule variant. The curate document (stock, filters, curated set) is edited through a 3-column UI: left = filtered pool table, middle = curated table (top) + 3D preview of last selection (bottom), right = 3D grid of all filtered kinds scaled to fit. Tables need +/- availability steppers and cross-window drag-and-drop, requiring extending the framework's declarative TableScene/table-host (React + wgpu parity) with typed cells, selection, sort, and drag/drop support. Register the new technology across Cargo.toml, package.json, repo/lib/js/index.ts, framework/core/js/index.ts, launch.json files, and s/manifest/resources.manifest.json.
summary: Live-reproduced the reported "graph edits revert after interaction ends" symptom across both the procedural (react) and trinity/media (react) node-graph surfaces. Root cause: a concurrent dev's in-progress edit to framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx dropped the `export { nodeGraphActions, textEditorActions };` re-export while still importing both for internal use. node-graph-host.tsx and text-editor-host.tsx import these two action-name maps from os-shell.tsx, so every module load threw `SyntaxError: The requested module ... os-shell.tsx does not provide an export named 'nodeGraphActions'`, caught by ShellRenderErrorBoundary, which remounted the whole tree from the last-committed document state — discarding any in-progress edit the instant the interaction (and the resulting re-render) completed. Confirmed on a freshly cold-started trinity-jack-react-dev server (ruling out stale Vite cache) and on procedural3d-react-dev. Fix: restored the missing re-export in os-shell.tsx. Re-verified live on both surfaces (render-error banner gone, slider drag + commit persists through the resync effect per [DEBUG] logs, no console errors) and ran the framework-renderer-react vitest suite (94/94 passing). Flow's node graph runs through a separate native WGPU canvas renderer (framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs) that doesn't depend on this React export path, so it was unaffected by this specific bug; no equivalent issue was found there. The July-11 fix for the original canvas-reattachment-storm bug (commit d6e56a6ff6) remains intact and was not the cause this time.
